scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A bridge carries thousands of heavy trucks across a river, without falling. How does it hold that weight?

scenes.name: forces
scenes.text: Every bridge balances two forces. Compression, which squeezes, and tension, which pulls.

scenes.name: beam
scenes.text: A beam bridge bends under load. The top gets squeezed and the bottom gets stretched.

scenes.name: arch
scenes.text: An arch turns the weight into compression, pushing outward and down into strong supports at each end.

scenes.name: suspension
scenes.text: A suspension bridge hangs the deck from huge cables in tension, draped over tall towers.

scenes.name: truss
scenes.text: Triangles called trusses spread the load, because a triangle can't change shape without changing a side.

scenes.name: movement
scenes.text: Bridges also have expansion joints, so they can grow and shrink with heat without cracking.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Compression, tension, smart shapes. Follow for more on how things really work.
